q: You are tired of re-explaining your job and writing style at the start of every chat. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Start each chat by pasting your full CV
Save a different prompt for every topic you discuss
Upgrade to a paid plan with better memory
Set custom instructions covering who you are, how you write and what to avoid
explanation: Custom instructions are a short profile that applies to every conversation, so each chat starts pre-briefed. Include who you are, how you write and what you never want in an output.

q: Which of these follows the lesson's template structure for a saved prompt?
options: "You are my editor. Here is my draft: ___. Make it tighter and more persuasive, same meaning, under ___ words."
"Rewrite this and make it better than before."
"What would you change about my writing?"
explanation: Saved prompts follow the Day 3 framework — role, context, task, format — with blanks for the parts that change. Three good templates beat thirty mediocre ones.

q: Why does the lesson suggest writing down the workflows you repeat, such as the weekly report or the Friday client email?
options: It is required before you can use custom instructions
It proves to your manager that you are organised
It becomes a personal playbook that saves time and travels with you to new tools
It lets you automate them with code later
explanation: A document of your repeatable workflows — the prompt, the tweaks, the output format — is your personal playbook. It takes an hour to build, saves hours every week, and comes with you if you switch tools.
